rows.title: A phone typed with an extension or a second number gets a clickable tel: link that dials a wrong, merged number
rows.summary: Now: contactHref's phone link (telHref in src/utils/contacts.js) dials the first number only, cut at '/', ',', ';', '|' or 'or' once seven digits are in (so '030/1234567' stays one number), with an extension (ext., extension, x, #) as RFC 3966 ';ext='. '+1 (555) 123-4567 ext. 890' links to tel:+15551234567;ext=890 and '+91 98765 43210 / +91 91234 56789' to tel:+919876543210, in the PDF, Word and Markdown. The printed text is unchanged. docs/knowledge/03-data-model.md notes it.

rows.title: A website/LinkedIn/GitHub 'Link URL' box holding only 'https://' (or 'www.') removes the contact's link, although the typed value is a good link
rows.summary: Now: a new linkOverride helper (src/utils/contacts.js) gives the Link URL only when safeHref accepts it. Otherwise ('https://', 'www.', a javascript: address) the box counts as empty, and contactHref links the typed value. The ATS text, cover-letter text and JSON Resume export use the same helper, so every format agrees. docs/knowledge/03-data-model.md notes it.
